scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem, and an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes bills will resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT.statement: A billing import validation rule change around August introduced a defect causing systematically wrong bills (e.g. mis-handling of read types or estimates).

H-AMI-MDMS-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI register reads are failing to arrive or validate correctly via the vendor's MDMS export, causing increased estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter reads from the contracted field service are not reliably reaching billing (handoff/semantic validity issue), increasing estimate substitution and bill errors.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Reduced field reading staffing/capacity since August lowered route completion rates, increasing missed reads and estimate-based billing errors.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of disputed bills, 1,785 (59%) had an ACTUAL read type and 1,240 (41%) had ESTIMATED, so the majority of disputes involve bills with a successfully recorded actual meter read, not estimate substitution (E-01).

Dispute ticket response times are well within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs a 3.0-day SLA, across 2,440 tickets). This indicates ticket-handling speed is not the bottleneck driving the dispute surge; the problem is more likely upstream (bill correctness) than downstream (response latency).

Field route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target across 9,200 manual-read accounts, showing a real but moderate (7pp) shortfall in manual meter-reading coverage during the dispute surge period.

The billing-db tariff change log returned zero records, indicating no tariff/rate changes were logged in the period, which rules out a tariff change as a cause of the wrong bills or dispute surge (E-04).

Monthly dispute counts show ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 (610, 590) roughly doubling to ~1,180-1,260/month in Aug-Sep 2026, confirming the scale of the surge referenced in the initial request. This is a volume trend only; it does not indicate which upstream cause (AMI delivery, field handoff, staffing, rule change) is responsible.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; this is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that happens to agree with the already-recorded authoritative billing-db tariff_change_log result (E-04=0), further corroborating that tariff change is not a cause of the wrong bills.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims the field reading contractor has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills instead of actual reads. This is an unverified stakeholder claim (not authoritative data) and SH-FIELD has a disclosed incentive to attribute problems to staffing (contract headcount increase).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) is an authoritative document confirming that route priority change requests from the utility are executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation; it corroborates the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint and says nothing about the cause of the billing dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log identifies 14 specific lagging manual-read routes (sample: route R-00 at 70% completion), providing route-level granularity under the aggregate 88% vs 95% completion shortfall already shown in E-03. It does not identify why these routes lag (staffing vs other causes) nor does it bear on billing read-type, rule-change, or AMI/MDMS causation.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db returned 320 accounts estimated in the last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (E-10), but the record only carries account_id and route — no read-type, validation-outcome, or handoff delivery/semantic-validity fields. So while complete as a dataset, it cannot by itself confirm or rule out AMI/MDMS delivery failure, field-handoff failure, or a billing rule defect as the cause of these estimates; it only shows the estimate problem is spread across far more routes (40) than the 14 lagging routes already identified in E-09.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.question: Does the billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES) show a specific validation rule change around August that explains wrong bills on both ACTUAL and ESTIMATED read accounts?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.decision_impact: This is the premise hypothesis H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT itself; until confirmed, no bill-correcting fix of any kind (automated or manual) should be deployed.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.resolution_path: Query billing-config (DA-RULES) for rule changes around August 2026 and cross-reference matched rule IDs against disputed bill records in DA-BILL/DA-TICKET.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.safe_placeholder: Treat H-RULE-CHANGE-DEFECT as unconfirmed; continue read-only diagnostic correlation only and do not deploy or recommend any bill-correcting change until the rule-change record is found.

U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.question: Once vendor-provisioned MDMS export access is available, do AMI read events for disputed-ESTIMATED accounts show delivery/validation failures, or are reads arriving correctly?
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Determines whether the vendor AMI/MDMS pipeline is a contributing cause distinct from the billing import rule defect, affecting which organization owns the remediation.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Await Telemetrix vendor-provisioned MDMS export access (currently ACCESS_PENDING; mdms-export tool DEGRADED with no fallback per recovery HOLD), then query AMI read events for disputed-ESTIMATED accounts.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Proceed with diagnostics using billing-db, crm-tickets and route-log data only; mark any MDMS-dependent conclusion as pending until vendor access is granted.

U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.question: Is the reported field reader shortage and 88% vs 95% route-completion shortfall a material contributor to the 41% ESTIMATED-read disputes, or incidental given SH-FIELD's disclosed headcount incentive?
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Affects whether any route-priority change is warranted at all, versus the surge being fully explained by the rule-change defect.
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Directly join incomplete-route accounts in DA-ROUTE against disputed-ESTIMATED accounts in DA-BILL/DA-TICKET rather than relying on SH-FIELD's unverified staffing claim (E-07).
U-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Treat field staffing/route completion as a secondary candidate only; do not push any route priority change based on SH-FIELD's claim alone, pending correlation.

U-HANDOFF-INTEGRITY.question: Are the field-to-billing and MDMS-to-billing handoffs delivering/validating reads correctly, given delivery_status and semantic_validity are currently UNKNOWN?
U-HANDOFF-INTEGRITY.decision_impact: If either handoff is failing, dispute causation could be partly handoff-driven rather than purely a billing import rule defect, changing which system needs remediation.
U-HANDOFF-INTEGRITY.resolution_path: Inspect delivery_status and semantic_validity logs for H-FIELD-BILL (daily upload) and H-MDMS-BILL (nightly export) once billing-config/mdms-export access permits.
U-HANDOFF-INTEGRITY.safe_placeholder: Treat both handoffs as unverified; do not attribute dispute causation to handoff failure, and keep review_handoff_integrity actions read-only/diagnostic only.

A-DATA-REPRESENTATIVENESS.statement: Disputed-bill read-type counts and route-completion figures are assumed representative of the broader population despite DA-BILL and DA-ROUTE completeness being marked UNKNOWN.
